title: Introduce scoring shim and per-client tuning to stabilize embedding scores
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers and internal rerankers are seeing inconsistent ranking changes after we rolled out a normalization pass in the embeddings pipeline. Some clients expect dot-product behavior from older models while newer model variants assume cosine-normalized vectors. This mismatch yields apparent regressions in reranking quality and also complicates unit-cost comparisons (dot scores are scale-dependent).

Goal: Ship a server-side scoring shim and a per-client tuning guide so we can: (1) preserve behavioral compatibility for legacy clients, (2) make a clear path for migration to cosine-normalized scoring, and (3) limit latency and cost impact. We want a transparent, observable bridge rather than a brittle client-side migration deadline.

Design summary (high level):
- Add a lightweight scoring_shim module in the embeddings service that transforms raw embedding vectors or scores into one of three modes per request: "legacy-dot", "cosine-normalized", or "auto-rescale".
- Support an explicit request header/SDK option: "embed-score-mode" (values: legacy-dot | cosine-normalized | auto-rescale). If absent, default will be the existing production behavior (legacy-dot) for backward compatibility for 6 months.
- The "auto-rescale" mode inspects the incoming vector L2 norm distribution vs model catalog norm expectations and applies a per-request multiplier to align magnitudes before dot scoring, effectively emulating cosine without dividing by norm (cheaper numerically).
- Provide server-side per-client overrides in routing rules so enterprise customers can opt-in to cosine-normalized scoring at their account level.
- Add telemetry: embed.norm.mean, embed.norm.std, embed.score.transform.type, and embed.score.delta to track differences between legacy and normalized outputs.
- Add SDK changes and examples documenting the header and migration checklist.

Technical trade-offs:
- Full cosine requires explicit normalization (divide by norm) which incurs a small additional compute cost; auto-rescale uses a scalar multiplier inferred from catalog stats to avoid per-vector division in the hot path, reducing CPU/GPU overhead at the cost of being an approximation for rare outliers.
- Defaulting to legacy-dot preserves stability but extends the period where new clients may not see improved ranking quality unless they opt-in.

Non-goals:
- Do not change model training or stored embedding formats. Do not require client-side re-encoding. This is a serving-layer compatibility shim only.

Why this is different from previous tickets: wording and approach emphasize an explicit per-request header and an "auto-rescale" approximation path that aims to keep latency impact <0.2ms per request while providing observable metrics to drive opt-ins. The migration plan centers on per-customer opt-in and telemetry-driven recommendations rather than immediate global switches.
acceptance_criteria: runtime exposes scoring_shim module and responds to embed-score-mode header with three supported modes: legacy-dot, cosine-normalized, auto-rescale
SDKs (py and js) can set embed-score-mode and include example migration snippets in docs
telemetry events produced: embed.norm.mean, embed.norm.std, embed.score.transform.type, embed.score.delta
end-to-end integration test showing numeric equivalence within tolerance between auto-rescale and explicit cosine for 99% of sampled inputs
performance: additional latency introduced by scoring_shim must be <0.2ms P95 on production-like hardware for 512-d vectors
rollout runbook validated with canary steps and automatic rollback criteria if customer-facing error rate increases by >1%
migration guide published with per-customer recommendation engine using collected telemetry
